title: Union with Christ in Salvation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Union with Christ in salvation means that every saving blessing is received because the believer belongs to Jesus Christ. Those united to Him share in His death, resurrection, righteousness, life, and hope.
summary: Union with Christ in salvation means that every saving blessing is received because the believer belongs to Jesus Christ. Those united to Him share in His death, resurrection, righteousness, life, and hope.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is not merely the giver of salvation benefits; He is the Savior to whom believers are joined. In Him, they receive forgiveness, righteousness, adoption, sanctification, perseverance, and glory.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Union with Christ is one of the richest truths of salvation. Believers are blessed in Christ, chosen in Christ, redeemed in Christ, made alive in Christ, and raised with Christ.

This union is spiritual and real. It does not make believers divine, but joins them to the risen Savior by faith through the work of the Spirit. Their identity and future are now bound to Him.

Because believers are united to Christ, His death counts for them and His resurrection life becomes theirs. They are no longer defined by Adam, sin, condemnation, or the old life as their final identity.

Union with Christ gathers many salvation doctrines together. Justification, adoption, sanctification, perseverance, and glorification are not disconnected gifts; they are blessings received in the beloved Son.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers try to understand salvation as a list of benefits detached from Jesus Himself. Union with Christ reminds them that the greatest gift of salvation is belonging to the Savior.

This doctrine gives deep identity to people who feel rejected, ashamed, addicted, disabled, forgotten, or disqualified. In Christ, the believer is not standing alone before God. He belongs to the Son.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live from your union with Christ. Count yourself dead to sin and alive to God. Do not define yourself by shame, failure, disability, addiction history, or human approval. Look to Christ as your life, and let belonging to Him shape your repentance, obedience, worship, and hope.
